description: Battle Rules 131.1 step 3 says 'Remove all expired temporary effects and tags' but no rule defines how tags are marked temporary or when they expire. Need a general Temporary Tag definition with expiry conditions in Entity System Rules 200.2.
title: GDD: Temporary tag expiry mechanism undefined

title: PoC: Audit existing code vs PoC.md

description:
Implement the 100x200 battlefield scene with deployment zones, zoom levels, and grid markers as described in PoC.md.

## Context
Support drag/multi-select of simple unit representations into the player's deployment zone; keep visuals minimal but clean.
title: PoC: Implement Battlefield scene

description:
Create the basic Engagement stage loop: planning movement/pivot orders, displaying movement previews, and executing orders with a basic enemy behavior as per PoC.md.

## Context
Focus on deterministic, debuggable logic; animations can be simple but should clearly show order execution.
title: PoC: Implement Engagement turn loop

description:
Add a persistent Menu button (and F10 hotkey) to relevant scenes (Sector Map, Armybuilding, Battlefield) providing Main Menu, Settings, Exit, and contextual options as described in Main Concepts and PoC.md.

## Context
Ensure this feels consistent across the prototype, even if Settings itself is minimal right now.
title: PoC: Implement persistent Menu button

description: Rosters are defined as Zones but are actually validation schemas. Zones answer 'where is this Entity?' while Rosters answer 'does this Battleforce meet requirements?' Proposal: Make Roster a Validation Schema Entity with RosterRequirementsComponent; add RosterValidationComponent to Battleforces; separate from Zone System. See Appendix B.7 in Entity System Rules.
title: Holdover: Roster as Zone (270.3) — separate validation from Zone concept

description: Campaign Rules 822.5 option 2 specifies percentage-based recovery of destroyed Units but doesn't define rounding for fractional results (e.g., 3 Units at 50%% = 1.5). Also unclear if recovered Units are restored to full Model count. Add rounding rule and recovery scope.
title: GDD: Campaign Partial Recovery fractional handling undefined

description: Battle Rules 133.5 step 2 distributes attacks to 'the closest Model in the target Unit' but provides no tiebreaker when multiple Models are equidistant. Non-deterministic. Add tiebreaker (e.g., lowest remaining Durability, then lowest ID).
title: GDD: Attack distribution tiebreaker for equidistant Models undefined

description: Datasheets are defined as a rules-level concept (240.5) but are purely a UI projection of Component data. No System reads or writes a Datasheet. Proposal: Remove rule 240.5, relocate field list to UI/presentation docs, update Terminology entry. See Appendix B.1 in Entity System Rules.
title: Holdover: Datasheets (240.5) — reclassify as UI view, not game rule

description: Orders are Unit-level but Combat resolves Model-by-Model; position is dual-level (Unit absolute, Model relative). This hybrid exists from tabletop conventions. Proposal: Document the design rationale explicitly if keeping (recommended), or evaluate fully Unit-level or fully Model-level alternatives. See Appendix B.8 in Entity System Rules.
title: Design review: Model-Unit resolution hybrid — document rationale or simplify

description: The Bearer relationship adds tabletop-derived indirection over standard ECS Component references. Proposal: Replace with explicit reference semantics in EquippedItemsComponent, state non-propagation as general ECS principle, retain Bearer as glossary convenience term only. See Appendix B.2 in Entity System Rules.
title: Holdover: Bearer relationship (230.2) — simplify to ECS reference semantics

description: Several Campaign Rules subsystems (Armybuilding 821, Narrative Event 823, Trade 825, Objectives 830, Scoring 840, Modifiers 850) lack explicit Examples sections with the setup/action/result format required by the documentation standard.
title: Campaign Rules: Add Examples sections to Activities, Objectives, and Scoring

description: Active Play currently uses synchronized Campaign Rounds (all players issue orders simultaneously, resolve, repeat). This is a tabletop convention. Evaluate: asynchronous turn-based (players act on their own schedule with notifications), real-time with pause, event-driven progression (advance time when all pending activities resolve), or hybrid models. The document already mentions free-form navigation as an alternative — formalize the design of that option and determine whether Rounds should be the default or the exception.
title: Campaign Rules: Evaluate Campaign Rounds for digital-native time model

description: Melee is defined both as a state Units are 'placed in' (132.2e) and a spatial condition 'within 1 distance unit' (glossary). Need to define Melee as a tracked tag: when applied, when removed, whether spatial check or explicit tag.
title: GDD: Melee state ambiguity (tag vs spatial condition)

description: Battle Rules 120.4 says 'Units with rules granting Pre-Engagement Movement may execute those moves' without specifying which Component or Ability Component provides this capability. This is a tabletop holdover where special rules are described in prose rather than structured Components. Should be formalized as a specific Passive Ability Component type (e.g., PreEngagementMoveAbility) with Movement System integration, processed by the Deployment System during rule 120.4.
title: Formalize Pre-Engagement Movement as Ability Component pattern

description: Unit tag inheritance from Models is a tabletop shortcut. In digital, Systems can query Model Components directly. Proposal: Replace inheritance rule with explicit System queries (any-Model or all-Model semantics), optionally maintain computed cache for performance. See Appendix B.3 in Entity System Rules.
title: Holdover: Tag Inheritance (240.3) — replace with System-level queries

description: The Sector Map is currently a discrete graph of Plots connected by Connections with integer Travel Costs — a direct analog of a board game map. Evaluate whether a continuous or hex-based territory system, procedural map generation, or a hybrid approach (graph for campaign layer, continuous for battlefield) would better serve the digital experience. Consider: discovery/fog-of-war mechanics, dynamic map evolution (Plots/Connections added/removed by narrative), and how spatial relationships between Plots affect strategy.
title: Campaign Rules: Evaluate board-game-style Sector Map for digital-native alternatives

description: Commanders currently move one Connection per Campaign Round with integer Travel Costs — a turn-based board game mechanic. Evaluate alternatives: real-time movement with pause, simultaneous movement with conflict resolution at meeting points, movement points per round allowing multi-hop traversal, or automated Commander movement (Commander sets a destination, Campaign System pathfinds). Also consider: should Commanders have Movement Components (speed, terrain modifiers) or is the current flat 1-connection-per-round sufficient?
title: Campaign Rules: Evaluate manual Commander movement for digital-native alternatives

description:
Finish and validate the Simple War GDD: reconcile terminology, complete stubs, add missing rules (battle, movement, campaign, entity system), and run documentation + rules validators.

## Context
High-level: Complete the Simple War game design document so that rules, terminology, and narrative foundations are coherent and ready for implementation. See Main Concepts, Terminology, Timeline, Gardener Subfactions, and Overarching Narrative for current state.
title: Epic: Finish Game Design Document

description:
Merge/deduplicate Overview/Terminology.md and Gameplay Rules/Terminology.md into a single authoritative terminology source. Ensure rule terms, entities, and phases are consistent and ready for documentation + rules validation.

## Context
Start here for GDD work. Read both terminology docs, list overlaps and conflicts, propose a merged outline, then update the files. After this, later tasks will run the documentation-standard and rules-validator skills.
title: GDD: Reconcile Terminology documents

description:
Use the Simple War Rules Validator skill on the completed rules sections (battle, movement, campaign, entities) to check logic, computability, and conflicts.

## Context
This is the final quality gate before treating GDD rules as implementation-ready. Capture any errors or warnings as new beads issues linked via discovered-from.
title: GDD: Run rules validator pass

description: Write a short ECS architecture appendix in Entity System Rules: define Entity as ID; catalog Component types (Position, Statline, Faction, Equipment, Morale, Zone, etc.); catalog Systems (Movement, Combat, Morale, Deployment, Campaign); map current Tags to Components or marker components; map existing Entities (Unit, Model, Item, Commander, Army, Campaign, Plot, Connection, Activity) to ECS archetypes. This becomes the reference for all subsequent ECS tasks.
title: ECS: Architecture design document

description: Rewrite Game Design Document/Gameplay Rules/Entity System Rules.md top to bottom using ECS concepts: replace Entity/Tag definitions with Entity/Component/System; redefine Entity Tags and Status Tags as marker and state components; redefine Characteristics as StatlineComponent; redefine Items, Models, Units as ECS entities and archetypes; update glossary and implementation notes with ECS state/system requirements.
title: ECS: Rewrite Entity System Rules

description: Review Entity System Rules for tabletop-derived concepts (Datasheets, model-level resolution, tag inheritance, bearer relationship, etc.), propose digital-native alternatives, and create follow-up beads issues (discovered-from this task) for each holdover that should be changed or revisited.
title: ECS: Review tabletop holdovers in Entity System

description: Update Gameplay Rules/Terminology.md to use ECS terminology consistently: replace Entity/Tag language with Component/System language; update Zone definitions (zones as components/systems, not 'like tags'); update Combat Resolution terminology to describe ECS data flow; ensure cross-references and rule numbers align with the new Entity System Rules.
title: ECS: Update Terminology.md

description: Update Gameplay Rules/Battle Rules.md to align with ECS: replace 'entity with the Battle tag' patterns with ECS archetype language; change state tracking to refer to components; review simultaneous resolution in terms of ECS system pipelines; review and flag any remaining tabletop holdovers in the battle flow for follow-up issues.
title: ECS: Update Battle Rules

description: Update Gameplay Rules/Campaign Rules.md for ECS: replace 'Entity with X tag' patterns for Campaign, Sector Map, Plot, Connection, Activity; express Campaign Modifiers as system overrides or component modifications; review tabletop holdovers (boardgame-style sector map, manual commander movement, etc.) and create follow-up issues for digital-native alternatives.
title: ECS: Update Campaign Rules

description: Update Gameplay Rules/Movement and Positioning Rules.md for ECS: replace tag-based terrain references with terrain components; align movement and footprint logic with ECS entities/components; review formations, footprints, deployment zones, and other spatial mechanics for tabletop holdovers and digital-native alternatives, creating follow-up issues as needed.
title: ECS: Update Movement & Positioning Rules

close_reason: Updated Main Concepts with ECS architecture framing: added Entity/Component/System section with archetype and System tables, updated all gameplay sections to use ECS vocabulary while preserving player-facing UX framing
description: Update Game Design Document/Overview/Main Concepts to describe the game in terms of the new ECS architecture (entities as IDs, components as data, systems as behavior), while preserving the player-facing UX framing for campaigns, armies, battles, and editors.
title: ECS: Update Main Concepts overview

description: Update src/data/*.json and src/data/loaders/*.gd to align with the new ECS terminology and structure where it makes sense: ensure Units, Models, Items, Attacks, Scenarios, and Godot data classes map cleanly onto ECS components/archetypes and that field names and comments reference ECS terminology.
title: ECS: Align data files and loaders

description:
Fill in the Main Concepts stubs for Armybuilding, Campaign Editor, Unit Editor, Settings, and Exit Game using the style and structure of existing Quickplay/Skirmish/Story/Multiplayer sections.

## Context
After terminology reconciliation, extend Game Design Document/Overview/Main Concepts so all main menu options have human-readable UX descriptions that align with PoC.md and future campaign plans.
title: GDD: Complete Main Concepts stubs

description:
Expand Game Design Document/Narrative Elements/Gardeners/Subfactions.md for Voidfarers, Cradle, and The Lost and the Damned, using Overarching Narrative.md as the primary source.

## Context
Fill in the remaining Gardener subfactions so factions are playable and narratively grounded. Keep each subfaction aligned with the broader Law/Ruin/World Tree arcs and how they might appear as in-game factions.
title: GDD: Write Gardener subfaction details

description:
Flesh out Game Design Document/Narrative Elements/Timeline.md from One Small Step through the End of All Things, with dates, short summaries, and cross-references into Overarching Narrative.md and faction sections.

## Context
Produce a timeline that designers and writers can use to place campaigns and short stories. Emphasize eras that will matter for story campaigns and in-game content.
title: GDD: Expand Timeline

description:
Write a Battle Rules section that formalizes the Planning, Deployment, Engagement, and Consolidation stages, with emphasis on the true simultaneous turn system (orders, reactions, resolution).

## Context
Use Main Concepts, Terminology, and PoC.md to define a computable, codable turn structure suitable for the current prototype and scalable later.
title: GDD: Draft Battle Rules (simultaneous turns)

description:
Specify how units and models move and face on the battlefield: grid size, measurement (e.g., Manhattan vs Euclidean), deployment zones, reinforcements, and restrictions.

## Context
Align with PoC.md battlefield spec (100x200 board, deployment zones, movement previews) and future complexity (formations, pathfinding).
title: GDD: Draft Movement and Positioning rules

description:
Write Campaign rules covering sector map structure, activities (Armybuilding, Battle, Narrative Events), objectives, scoring, and how campaigns modify battles.

## Context
Grounded in Main Concepts, PoC.md, and existing narrative; output should be detailed enough to design the quickplay campaign and future story campaigns.
title: GDD: Draft Campaign Rules

description:
Formalize rules for Commanders, Units, Models, Items, Characteristics, Tags, and Abilities, turning terminology into numbered rules that are ready for validation and future codegen.

## Context
Use Gameplay Rules/Terminology.md plus src/data/*.json as references. Focus on what must be true in all implementations (tabletop and digital).
title: GDD: Draft Entity System rules

description:
Apply the Simple War Documentation Standard skill to all GDD markdown: fix numbering, headers, cross-references, and glossary entries.

## Context
Run this after all major GDD sections are drafted. Output: a report of issues and applied fixes, plus any follow-up tasks for deeper structural changes.
title: GDD: Run documentation-standard validation

description: Movement Rules 320.1 says 'the footprint may shrink as remaining Models consolidate' — 'may' is ambiguous (optional? automatic?). Reword to specify footprint recalculates automatically based on remaining Model count and formation.
title: GDD: Unit footprint 'may shrink' ambiguity on Model destruction

description: armour_type: string is a required field in ArmourComponent with no defined mechanical effect. No System reads it. Proposal: Either remove (presentation-only), promote to marker Component on Item Entity for rule targeting, or define Combat/Ability System interactions. See Appendix B.5 in Entity System Rules.
title: Holdover: Armour Type (220.6) — define mechanical role or remove

description: State inheritance (Unit inherits state when all Models share it) is an aggregation rule disguised as inheritance. Only one example given (destruction), scope undefined. Proposal: Define explicit System aggregation conditions per state, enumerate all inheritable states. See Appendix B.4 in Entity System Rules.
title: Holdover: State Inheritance (240.4) — replace with explicit System aggregation

description:
Turn the Overarching Narrative prompts into structured short story skeletons (characters, arcs, key scenes, themes) across all eras, to feed future campaign and in-game narrative design.

## Context
High-level: Use Overarching Narrative.md (especially the Story Prompts section) to create reusable outlines that connect lore, factions, and game mechanics at a personal scale. These skeletons become building blocks for campaign design (Epic 5).
title: Epic: Short Story Skeletons

description: Entity System Rules 210.3 says sub-lethal damage is tracked for future resolution but no rule specifies when or how it resolves. Does damage accumulate across turns? Add explicit accumulation or per-instance resolution rule.
title: GDD: Sub-lethal damage accumulation undefined

description:
Analyze curated Godot and related repos (ECS, RTS, movement, projectiles, multiplayer, modding) plus a small number of additional examples, then synthesize concrete design recommendations for Simple War.

## Context
High-level: Use Repositories.md under Game Design Document/Useful Examples as the curated starting point. Extract patterns that directly inform Simple War's architecture (src/README.md) and PoC implementation (PoC.md), especially around entity systems, battle scale, movement, and UX.
title: Epic: Godot Repo Analysis

description:
Deep dive into nilpunch/massive-ecs. Evaluate whether an ECS pattern fits Simple War's entity needs (Commanders, Units, Models, Items, Tags, Abilities) versus Godot-native node/resource patterns. Document trade-offs and recommendations.

## Context
Start here for repo analysis. Read Game Design Document terminology + src/README.md entity plans, then study massive-ecs. Output should be a short design note: where ECS helps, where it complicates Godot workflows, and whether to adopt fully, partially, or not at all.
title: Research: ECS and entity architecture (massive-ecs)

description:
Study Beyond All Reason and godot-open-rts for structural patterns: battle scenes, unit management at scale, AI opponent loops, and save/load. Extract ideas that translate well to Simple War's simultaneous battles and campaign layer.

## Context
Read PoC.md and src/README.md first, then focus on how these projects organize large battles and game state. Output: notes with code links and concrete suggestions for Simple War's battle/campaign architecture.
title: Research: RTS structure and scale (BAR + godot-open-rts)

description:
Deep dive into rtsSelectionMoveDemo for unit selection, drag/multi-select, formation movement, and pathfinding. Map patterns directly to Simple War's order planning and movement preview needs.

## Context
Output should include concrete UX and code patterns we want to emulate in the PoC battlefield and later systems.
title: Research: Movement, selection, and formations (rtsSelectionMoveDemo)

description:
Study godot-blast-bullets-2d for performance-conscious projectile and collision handling. Evaluate how much of this we need for Simple War's combat visualization in the near term.

## Context
Focus on patterns we might adopt later; near-term PoC can be simpler, but design choices now should avoid blocking this later.
title: Research: Projectiles and combat visuals (godot-blast-bullets-2d)

description:
Analyze Godot-Lobby and Godot-Universal-Mod-Manager for patterns we might adopt for Simple War's multiplayer modes and future content/mod support.

## Context
This is forward-looking; outcome is a short recommendation on whether to lean on these projects or roll custom solutions later.
title: Research: Multiplayer and modding foundations

description:
Search for a small set of additional Godot 4.x repos that fill gaps not covered by Repositories.md: turn-based tactics, hex/grid implementations, narrative-heavy games, or data-driven unit definitions. Append useful finds to Repositories.md.

## Context
Keep this focused and bounded (e.g., +3–5 repos). The goal is to round out examples, not boil the ocean.
title: Research: Additional Godot examples

description:
Cross-reference findings from all research tasks against Simple War's architecture (src/README.md) and PoC.md. Produce a ranked list of patterns to adopt, with rationale and which system each affects (entities, battles, movement, AI, multiplayer, modding).

## Context
This task distills research into decisions. Its output should directly inform PoC and later systems.
title: Synthesis: Repo-derived design recommendations

description:
Create a design patterns reference document under Game Design Document/Useful Examples/ summarizing the adopted patterns from analyzed repos, with links and brief code references.

## Context
Intended as a living reference for anyone working on Simple War's Godot code. Keep sections short and focused on how/why to apply each pattern.
title: Doc: Godot design patterns for Simple War

description: Equipment limitations are prose-defined ('a Model may equip at most one heavy_plate Armour'). Not machine-readable. Proposal: Introduce EquipmentConstraintsComponent or EquipmentSlotComponent with structured constraint data; create Equipment Validation System. See Appendix B.6 in Entity System Rules.
title: Holdover: Equipment constraints (230.2, 240.2) — formalize as Components

description: The Lawmakers General Overview contains a truncated sentence: 'lost touch with .' — the object of 'with' is missing. Needs author input to complete.
title: Subfactions.md: Complete Lawmakers incomplete sentence

description: Reposition Reaction (133.3a) taxes Endurance by 1 but there's no requirement that the Unit has remaining Endurance. Rule 132.4 only gates Orders, not Reactions. A Unit with 0 Endurance can Reposition. Add 'must have at least 1 remaining Endurance' to Reposition requirements.
title: GDD: Reposition Reaction missing Endurance gate

description: Movement Rules (300-series) now make forward references to terrain Entities with Blocking, Grounded marker Components and spatial extent Components. These references need a home: draft the Terrain Rules (600-series) defining terrain Entity archetypes, terrain Components (spatial extent, passability, LOS effects), marker Components (Blocking, Grounded, etc.), and terrain interaction rules for the Movement System and Combat System.
title: GDD: Draft Terrain Rules (600-series) for terrain Entity archetypes and Components

description: Four rules documents (Battle Rules, Entity System Rules, Movement Rules, Campaign Rules) each have their own Glossary Additions sections with overlapping entries. Consolidate into a single master glossary document (900-series) and convert per-document glossaries to references.
title: Create unified master glossary consolidating per-document Glossary Additions

description: Movement Rules 320.3 defines only rectangular_block as a formation type. A digital game can support richer formation types (wedge, spread, line, diamond, staggered) that would affect footprint shape, cohesion, and gameplay. Evaluate which formation types add meaningful tactical depth vs complexity, define their FormationComponent representations, and specify how the Movement System computes FootprintComponent for each. Related to Godot research bead simple-war-nby.3 (formations).
title: GDD: Expand FormationComponent beyond rectangular_block for digital-native alternatives

description: Battle Rules use 'placed in Melee' (132.2e, 134.1) as an implicit proximity state with no Component representation. In ECS, Melee should be formalized as either a marker Component (InMelee Status Tag) or a Zone state, with explicit rules for how the Combat System sets and clears it. Currently Melee is only defined by proximity (within 1 distance unit) which is a tabletop holdover.
title: Formalize Melee as ECS Component or Zone

description:
Design a cohesive set of story campaigns set during the End of All Things, using the established factions and lore to drive gameplay across multiple perspectives.

## Context
High-level: Build on the End of All Things section and Story Prompts in Overarching Narrative.md plus the finalized Timeline to define 3–5 interlocking story campaigns (e.g., human Preservers, Choir, Torn, Stewards, Gardeners). Each campaign should have clear motivations, conflicts, and multiple endings tied to game outcomes.
title: Epic: End-Times Campaign Story

description: Endurance is defined as a Model-level Characteristic (210.1) but all Battle Rules track it at the Unit level. If Models have different Endurance values, the Unit's Endurance is undefined. Need explicit resolution rule.
title: GDD: Endurance scope ambiguity (Model characteristic vs Unit tracking)

description: The canonical Terminology document has no rule numbering. Assign 900-series rule numbers to all sections so other documents can cross-reference by rule number instead of prose references.
title: Terminology.md: Assign 900-series rule numbers

description: Battle Rules reference 'line of sight' in Order types (132.2a Hold, 132.2b Advance, 132.2f Dig In) but LOS is never defined. This is a tabletop holdover where LOS is typically eyeballed or measured with a ruler. Needs formalization as a System query (e.g., the Combat System checks LOS between PositionComponents, considering Blocking terrain marker Components) with clear algorithmic definition for digital.
title: Define Line of Sight rules for digital implementation

description: Battle Rules 134.1 step 1 says 'Units in Melee that have not yet attacked this Turn exchange attacks.' A Unit that Hold-attacked during 133.5 and was then Charged into Melee cannot defend itself. Reword to allow both ranged and melee combat as independent events.
title: GDD: Melee participation after ranged attack interaction unclear

description: Baseline Competence (210.7a) and Evasion Rating (210.7b) defer their derivations to Combat Resolution rules (400-series) which do not exist. The hit probability formula (133.5 step 3) is uncomputable without these. Either draft 400-series or provide interim formulas.
title: GDD: Combat Resolution derivations undefined (Baseline Competence, Evasion Rating formulas)
